claims.text: The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy is comprised mainly of Mo, Nb, Ta, and W.
Adding approximately 5 wt% Al will promote formation of a continuous Al2O3 scale during high-temperature exposure.
The Al2O3 scale formed after Al addition will be adherent.
Formation of the Al2O3 scale will significantly improve oxygen resistance relative to the untreated alloy.
At high temperatures, Al oxidizes preferentially in this alloy.
Preferential oxidation of Al forms a stable Al2O3 layer.
The Al2O3 layer acts as a barrier that reduces oxygen ingress.
The Al2O3 barrier prevents formation of non-protective, spallation-prone oxide scales.
Under the specified exposure, the Al-modified alloy will have lower oxidation weight gain than the untreated alloy.
Under the specified exposure, the Al-modified alloy will develop a more uniform oxide-scale morphology than the untreated alloy.
Under the specified exposure, the Al-modified alloy will exhibit better oxide-scale adhesion than the untreated alloy.
The untreated alloy has poor oxidation resistance under extreme-temperature conditions.
The poor oxidation resistance of the untreated alloy is caused by formation and spallation of non-protective oxide scales.
The predicted benefit is expected after approximately 100 hours at approximately 1200°C in the stated oxygen-rich atmosphere.

contradictions.description: The atmosphere is described as both ambient air and 1 atm O2. Ambient air at 1 atm total pressure has an oxygen partial pressure of about 0.21 atm, whereas 1 atm O2 denotes essentially pure oxygen; thus the test atmosphere is internally inconsistent.
